beliefs: f is even: f(-x)=f(x) to within noise [E1, E2, E3]
The linear slope is slightly sublinear at very large |x|: f(127)=2131.6 vs 16.79·127=2132, and f(128)=2151.2 vs 2149 — close enough to linear [E1]
There is a special interval roughly |x| < 1 where f deviates strongly from the linear law, with a sharp dip near x=0 [E3]
The near-zero region is noisy/erratic (e.g. f(0.1)=1.65 vs f(0.15)=0.33), so exact values there are unpredictable; only the envelope is captured [E3]
The transition from the near-zero dip to the linear regime happens around |x|≈0.5-1 [E3]
notes: Replaced the quadratic+small-bump model with a linear law 16.79·|x| for |x|>=~1, and a noisy near-zero region modeled as a smooth ramp that dips to ~0.75 at 0 and rises to meet the linear law by |x|≈1; the erratic values near 0 are treated as noise.
